<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">PART I</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 36pt">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Item 1</font>.</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">BUSINESS</font></font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">General</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Syms Corp (&#8221;Syms&#8221; or the &#8220;Company&#8221;) and its wholly-owned subsidiary Filene&#8217;s Basement, LLC (&#8220;Filene&#8217;s&#8221;, &#8220;Filene&#8217;s, LLC&#8221; or &#8220;Filene&#8217;s Basement&#8221;) collectively own and operate a chain of 47 &#8220;off-price&#8221; retail stores under the &#8220;Syms&#8221; name (which are owned and operated by the Company) and &#8220;Filene&#8217;s Basement&#8221; name (which are owned and operated by Filene&#8217;s, LLC).&#160;&#160;The stores are located in the United States throughout the Northeastern and Middle Atlantic regions and in the Midwest, Southeast and Southwest.&#160;&#160;Each Syms store offers a broad range of first quality, in-season merchandise bearing nationally recognized designer or brand-name labels for men, women and children at prices substantially lower than those generally found in department and specialty stores.&#160;&#160;On June 18, 2009, the Company&#8217;s, wholly-owned subsidiary, SYL, LLC now known as Filene&#8217;s Basement, LLC acquired certain real property leases, inventory, equipment and other assets of Filene&#8217;s Basement Inc. (&#8220;Filene&#8217;s Inc.&#8221; or &#8220;Filene&#8217;s Basement Inc.&#8221;), a retail clothing chain, pursuant to an auction conducted in accordance with &#167; 363 of the Federal Bankruptcy Code.&#160;&#160;As a result, Filene&#8217;s, LLC owns and operates 21 Filene&#8217;s Basement stores that are located in the Northeastern, Middle Atlantic, Midwest and Southeast regions.&#160;&#160;Filene&#8217;s Basement also offers a broad range of first quality brand name and designer clothing for men, women and children.&#160;&#160;In addition, Syms owns and operates 5 co-branded Syms/Filene&#8217;s Basement stores.&#160;&#160;Syms and Filene&#8217;s, LLC operate in a single operating segment &#8211; the &#8220;off-price&#8221; retail stores segment.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The Company was incorporated in New Jersey in 1983.&#160;&#160;The Company maintains its headquarters at One Syms Way, Secaucus, New Jersey 07094, telephone (201) 902-9600.&#160;&#160;Unless otherwise noted, and notwithstanding that Syms Corp. owns and operates Syms and co-branded Syms/Filene&#8217;s Basement stores and Filene&#8217;s, LLC is a separate legal entity and owns and operates Filene&#8217;s Basement stores, references to the &#8220;Company&#8221;, &#8220;we&#8221; or &#8220;our&#8221; relate to Syms Corp, including its wholly-owned subsidiary Filene&#8217;s, LLC.&#160;&#160;Our fiscal year ends on the Saturday closest to the last day of February each year.&#160;&#160;Fiscal 2010 ended on February 26, 2011; fiscal 2009 ended on February 27, 2010, and fiscal 2008 ended on February 28, 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The discussion below is herein presented on a consolidated basis and includes information regarding the Company and its wholly-owned subsidiary Filene&#8217;s, LLC.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Description of Business</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The Company&#8217;s 47 stores offer a broad range of &#8220;off-price&#8221; first quality, in-season merchandise consisting primarily of, women&#8217;s dresses, suits, separates and accessories, men&#8217;s tailored clothing and haberdashery, children&#8217;s apparel, luggage, domestics and fragrances and shoes.&#160;&#160;The stores emphasize first quality, nationally recognized designer and brand name merchandise at prices substantially below those generally found in department and specialty stores.&#160;&#160;The stores carry a wide selection of sizes and styles of men&#8217;s, women&#8217;s and children&#8217;s wear.&#160;&#160;In addition several stores also carry a selection of fine jewelry.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The Company has no foreign operations.&#160;&#160;No material part of the Company&#8217;s revenues is received from a single customer or group of customers.&#160;&#160;Please refer to Note 1 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for information on segment reporting.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Merchandise</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Most of the items sold by the Company consist of nationally recognized designer and brand-name merchandise.&#160;&#160;Merchandise is generally displayed by department, class and size on conveniently arranged racks, fixtures, tables or counters.&#160;&#160;No emphasis is placed on any particular &#8220;label&#8221; or brand.&#160;&#160;Most stores offer minor alterations for an additional charge.</font></div>

<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Purchasing</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The Company purchases first quality, in-season, brand-name merchandise directly from manufacturers on terms it believes are more favorable than those generally obtained by department and specialty stores.&#160;&#160;We estimate that approximately 900 designer and brand-name manufacturers of merchandise are represented in our stores.&#160;&#160;The Company generally does not maintain large out-of-season inventories.&#160;&#160;However, we occasionally buy certain basic clothing which does not change in style from year to year at attractive prices for storage until the following season.&#160;&#160;Purchasing is performed by a buying staff in conjunction with Merchandise Managers.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Co-branding</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Company converted four former Syms stores (Norwood, MA, Berlin, CT, Elmsford, NY and Westbury, NY) to co-branded stores in fiscal 2010.&#160;&#160;In fiscal 2009, the Company converted one former Syms store (Fairfield, CT) to a co-branded store.&#160;&#160;These stores carry the names of both Syms and Filene&#8217;s Basement and combine the strengths of both brands with an expanded selection of women&#8217;s merchandise in the former Syms stores.&#160;&#160;We continue to monitor the customer reaction and store performance; at present, no additional locations have been identified for co-branding for fiscal 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Distribution</font></font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Company operates a 457,000 square foot leased distribution facility situated on 32.8 acres in Auburn, Massachusetts.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company owns a facility in Secaucus, New Jersey.&#160;&#160;This facility contains approximately 277,000 square feet of warehouse and distribution space, 34,000 square feet of office space and 29,000 square feet of store space.&#160;&#160;The facility is located on an 18.6 acre parcel of land for which the Company holds a ground lease for a remaining term of approximately 265 years.&#160;&#160;Since the acquisition of Filene&#8217;s in June 2009, the Company has continued to assess the most effective manner in which to integrate the operations of Filene&#8217;s and Syms to maximize the synergies of the two businesses.&#160;&#160;This plan included the consolidation of distribution center functions.&#160;&#160;The consolidation of distribution center functions involved a shift of most merchandise processing to the Company&#8217;s Massachusetts distribution center.&#160;&#160;The New Jersey distribution center will serve to replenish the high volume New York City stores and will continue to house the adjoining retail store and corporate offices.&#160;&#160;Most of the merchandise is processed and distributed from the Massachusetts distribution facility where it is received from manufacturers, inspected, ticketed and allocated to particular stores.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Marketing</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Company&#8217;s stores offer everyday low pricing in key fashion categories along with home goods and accessories.&#160;&#160;Syms stores have as their tagline &#8220;An Educated Consumer is Our Best Customer&#8221;&#8482;, one of the best known and longest lasting in retail.&#160;&#160;The Company believes that the Syms store customer is very loyal and appreciates and understands great brands at great prices.&#160;&#160;Filene&#8217;s Basement&#8217;s tagline, &#8220;Where Bargains Were Born&#8221;&#8482;, illustrates its long standing position as the original off-price retailer.&#160;&#160;The Company believes that the Filene&#8217;s Basement customer has a high fashion IQ and recognizes the value in what is being offered.&#160;&#160;We have continued to enhance the &#8220;Running of the Brides&#8221; events, a bridal gown event that is unique to Filene&#8217;s Basement and garners a great deal of media attention.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Company advertises principally on radio and occasionally on television.&#160;&#160;The Company also utilizes print and billboard ads, as well as direct mail and electronic media including e-mail communication to registered customers.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company utilizes social media to enable it to communicate immediately with its customer base.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Company&#8217;s policy is to affix a price ticket on most items displaying our selling price as well as the price the Company regards as the traditional full retail price of that item at department or specialty stores.&#160;&#160;All garments are sold with the brand-name as affixed by the manufacturer.&#160;&#160;We utilize vendor names and &#8220;our price, their price&#8221; on our in-store signage.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Company has historically had excellent, longstanding relationships with its suppliers.&#160;&#160;This has made us a preferred choice for vendors with designer and famous brand overruns, department store cancellations and unmet volume objectives.&#160;&#160;These vendors understand that goods will be sold in an environment that supports the stature of their brands.&#160;&#160;Our buyers are encouraged to purchase merchandise of the quality and names that our customers desire.</font></div>

<br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Competition</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The retail apparel business is highly competitive, and the Company accounts for only a small fraction of the total market for men&#8217;s, women&#8217;s and children&#8217;s apparel.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s stores compete with discount stores, specialty apparel stores, department stores, manufacturer-owned factory outlet stores and others.&#160;&#160;Many of the stores with which the Company competes are units of large national or regional chains that have substantially greater resources than the Company.&#160;&#160;Retailers having substantially greater resources than the Company have entered or have indicated their intention to enter the &#8220;off-price&#8221; apparel business, and the &#8220;off-price&#8221; apparel business itself has become increasingly competitive, especially with respect to the increased use by manufacturers of their own factory outlets and the use of on-line sites by other retailers.&#160;&#160;At various times of the year, department store chains and specialty shops offer brand-name merchandise at substantial markdowns.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Operations and Control Systems</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In 2010, the Company continued the integration of the Syms and Filene&#8217;s Basement management information systems onto one consolidated system platform.&#160;&#160;Product is tracked in approximately 450 different categories from its purchase to its ultimate sale in the Company&#8217;s stores.&#160;&#160;All information regarding the product is transmitted daily to the Company&#8217;s centralized databases.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s executives receive detailed reports regarding sales and inventory at both the unit and retail dollar level on a store-by-store basis daily.&#160;&#160;In addition, reports monitoring critical business processes are made available daily.&#160;&#160;In 2010, the Company completed deploying its Point of Sale system in all the Company&#8217;s stores, providing the flexibility needed to better service its customers and enhance their in-store experience.&#160;&#160;In 2011, the Company plans to upgrade its Allocation system in order to improve its ability to get the right product into the right store at the right time.</font></div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Management of the Company visits stores on a regular basis to evaluate store performance.&#160;&#160;During these visits, merchandise needs, visual displays, staffing and employee issues, statistical store performance, and loss prevention issues are reviewed.&#160;&#160;Stores have some combination of on-premises loss prevention or security personnel and various theft deterrent and prevention systems during normal hours and monitored security systems after hours.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Employees</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As of February 26, 2011, the Company had approximately 2,500 employees, of which approximately 1,400 work on a part time basis.&#160;&#160;Each store employs anywhere from approximately 30 to 160 associates, consisting mostly of sales personnel.&#160;&#160;Syms has collective bargaining agreements with Local 1102 and Local 108, both of the Retail Wholesale Department Store Workers Union (RWDSU).&#160;&#160;These contracts were renegotiated in 2010 and have expiration dates of October 31, 2013 and November 1, 2013, respectively.&#160;&#160;Syms also has a collective bargaining agreement with Local 400 of the United Food and Commercial Workers Union.&#160;&#160;This agreement was also renegotiated in 2010 with an expiration date of April 30, 2012.&#160;&#160;Combined, these three local unions represent approximately 850 hourly employees at the Syms store locations.&#160;&#160;In 2010, the majority of Filene&#8217;s Basement store employees voted to be represented by RWDSU Local 1102.&#160;&#160;A new agreement was negotiated which covers approximately 1,100 Filene&#8217;s Basement store employees and expires on June 21, 2012.&#160;&#160;The Company believes that its relationship with its unions and employees is good.</font></div>

<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">RISK FACTORS</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The following risk factors and other information included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K should be carefully considered.&#160;&#160;The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face.&#160;&#160;Additional risk and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial also may impair our business operations.&#160;&#160;If any of the following risks materialize, our business, financial condition, operating results and cash flows could be materially adversely affected.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have incurred losses in recent fiscal periods and may not be profitable in the short-term</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have experienced losses in recent fiscal periods and cannot guarantee that we will return to profitability in the short-term.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Deterioration in general economic conditions and the impact on consumer confidence and consumer spending could continue to materially and adversely impact our results of operations in future periods.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Consumer spending habits, including spending for our merchandise, are affected by, among other things, prevailing market conditions, levels of employment, salary and wage rates, declines in discretionary income and actual and perceived wealth, gasoline and energy costs, prevailing interest rates, income tax rates and policies, consumer confidence and consumer perception of general economic conditions. As a result of the prolonged deterioration in economic conditions worldwide over the past few years, consumer confidence and consumer spending have been negatively impacted and while economic conditions are showing signs of improvement, it is unclear whether any such improvements will continue or how significant the improvements will be. Consumer purchases of discretionary items, including our merchandise, can be expected to decline during periods when disposable income is adversely affected or there is economic uncertainty.&#160;&#160;We have been affected by these general economic conditions in the latest fiscal year and expect these conditions to affect our current and future fiscal periods.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We may be unable to compete favorably in our highly competitive markets</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The retail business is highly competitive and we account for only a small fraction of the total market for men&#8217;s, women&#8217;s and children&#8217;s apparel.&#160;&#160;We compete against discount stores, specialty apparel stores, department stores, manufacturer-owned factory outlet stores and others.&#160;&#160;Our success depends on our ability to remain competitive with respect to style, price, brand availability and customer service.&#160;&#160;The performance of our competitors, as well as changes in their pricing policies, marketing activities and other business strategies, could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and our market share.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">If we are unable to meet certain financial covenants in our credit facility, our ability to borrow could be constrained</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We had $30.2 million in borrowings as of the end of the current fiscal year under our existing credit agreement. The facility contains various covenants.&#160;&#160;While we are in compliance with these covenants and monitor such compliance, if in the future we continue to borrow monies under the facility and fail to meet these covenants or obtain appropriate waivers, our lender may terminate the credit facility or accelerate any then-existing debt.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our sales and operating results depend on consumer preferences and fashion trends</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our sales and operating results depend in part upon our ability to anticipate and respond to product and fashion trends as well as to anticipate, gauge and react to changing consumer demands in a timely manner.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance that the merchandise on hand or on order will correspond to changes in taste and demand or that we will be able to successfully secure and market merchandise that is responsive to such trends.&#160;&#160;Consumer demand requires us to anticipate and respond to numerous and fluctuating variables in fashion trends and other conditions in the markets in which our stores are situated.&#160;&#160;A variety of factors may affect our ability to maintain the proper mix of products in each store, including without limitation: variations in local, regional or national economic conditions which could affect our customers&#8217; discretionary spending, unanticipated fashion trends, our success in distributing merchandise to our stores in an efficient manner and changes in weather patterns, which in turn may affect consumer demand and preferences.&#160;&#160;If we misjudge the market for our products, or if we are unable to anticipate and fulfill the merchandise needs of each region, we may experience decreases in our sales, we may realize significant excess inventories for some products and we may be forced to increase markdowns in relation to slow-moving merchandise, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.</font></div>

<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">5</font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">If we are unable to renew or enter into new leases on favorable terms, our revenue growth may decline</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We operate 31 of our locations in leased premises.&#160;&#160;The leases for eight of these 31 locations expire during 2011 through 2013 and several are subject to extension or renewal, in the Company&#8217;s discretion.&#160;&#160;If the cost of leasing existing stores increases, we cannot assure you that we will be able to maintain our existing store locations as leases expire.&#160;&#160;In addition, we may not be able to enter into new leases on favorable terms or at all, or we may not be able to locate suitable alternative sites or additional new sites for new stores in a timely manner.&#160;&#160;Our revenues and earnings may decline if we fail to maintain existing store locations, enter into more costly new leases, locate alternative sites on more expensive terms or fail to find suitable additional sites for new stores.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our relationships with vendors can change</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We currently purchase first-quality, in-season designer and brand name merchandise from more than 900 vendors at prices we believe to be below those generally available to major department and specialty stores.&#160;&#160;Although we have maintained long-term business relationships with many of these vendors, there can be no assurance that we will be able to continue to purchase first-quality, in-season merchandise from these vendors in the same breadth of styles and sizes, in the same or greater volumes and at prices as favorable as those currently available to us.&#160;&#160;If we fail to maintain our relations with our existing vendors, or to enhance the quality of merchandise they supply us or if we cannot maintain existing sources of supply or attract new vendors of in-season brand name and designer merchandise, our ability to obtain a sufficient amount and variety of merchandise at favorable prices may be limited, which could have a significant negative impact on our competitive position and our results of operations could be materially and adversely affected.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, if we are unable to maintain or continue to obtain trade credit from factors, vendors and service providers on favorable terms, we may not be able to develop or enhance our merchandise or respond to competitive pressures, any of which could have a material adverse effect on our business.&#160;&#160;Further, the tightening of trade credit could limit our available liquidity.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our ability to manage inventory can affect our business</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The fashion-oriented nature of our products and the rapid changes in customer preferences leave us vulnerable to an increased risk of inventory obsolescence.&#160;&#160;Our ability to manage inventories properly is an important factor in our operations.&#160;&#160;Inherent in our management and valuation of inventories are certain significant judgments and estimates, including, among others, initial merchandise markup and subsequent markups and markdowns which significantly impact the ending inventory valuation at retail as well as the resulting cost complement.&#160;&#160;While management believes that these methods provide an inventory valuation which reasonably approximates cost, if market conditions are less favorable than those projected, additional markdowns may be required.&#160;&#160;If we are unable to effectively manage inventory, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially adversely affected.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our results may be adversely affected by increases in the price of raw materials, oil and other commodities</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Increases in the price of raw materials, oil and other commodities may reduce our overall profitability.&#160;&#160;Specifically, the cost of fabrics and other materials that are used in the manufacture of merchandise we purchase from our suppliers has recently risen significantly.&#160;&#160;Such increases are expected to increase the cost of merchandise, which could adversely offset our performance through potentially reduced consumer demand or reduced margins.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the price of oil has fluctuated dramatically in the past and recently risen significantly.&#160;&#160;An increase in the price of oil increases our transportation costs for distribution, utility costs for our retail stores and costs to purchase our products from suppliers.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Acquisitions involve special risk, including the risk that we may not be able to fully realize the benefits of any such acquisition</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In 2009, we acquired certain assets of Filene&#8217;s Basement, Inc.&#160;&#160;Realization of the expected return on the Filene&#8217;s acquisition, such as the anticipated revenue increases, cost savings and increases in geographic and product presence and customer reach resulting from the acquisition, has been limited thus far due to difficulties integrating the Filene&#8217;s assets and operations into our existing infrastructure and operations.&#160;&#160;In particular, we have experienced difficulties associated with data and platform integration in connection with our acquisition of Filene&#8217;s, which have, to date, limited the projected benefits of the acquisition.</font></div>

<br>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our failure to retain our existing senior management and to continue to attract qualified new personnel could adversely affect our business</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our success will depend on our ability to retain our key personnel and attract and retain talented, highly qualified executives.&#160;&#160;If we were to lose the benefit of the experience, efforts and abilities of any of our key executive and buying personnel, our business could be adversely affected.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, our success is also dependent on our ability to hire and train qualified retail management and associates. We are also subject to risks associated with any significant disruptions in our relationship with our employees and any work stoppages by our employees, including union employees.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We recorded a $4.3 million impairment charge during fiscal 2010 and may be required to recognize additional impairment charges in the future</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Pursuant to accounting principles generally accepted in the United States, we are required to periodically assess our long-lived assets to determine if they are impaired. Business disruptions, protracted economic weakness, declines in operating results and other factors may result in asset impairments. For the fiscal year ended February 26, 2011, the carrying amount of certain long-lived assets exceeded their implied fair values and as a result the Company recognized an impairment charge of $4,255,000. In fiscal 2009, we recorded an impairment charge of $80,000. In light of current economic conditions, additional impairments could occur in future periods whether or not connected to the current impairment analysis. Future impairment charges could materially and adversely affect our reported earnings in the periods of such charges and could materially and adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are subject to potential uninsured losses and/or claims</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are subject to the possibility of uninsured losses from risks such as terrorism, earthquake or floods, for which no, or limited, insurance coverage is maintained.&#160;&#160;We are also subject to risk of losses which may arise from adverse litigation results or other claims.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Changes in governmental regulation could adversely affect our operations</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Laws and regulations at both state and federal levels frequently change and the ultimate cost of compliance cannot be precisely estimated. In addition, we cannot predict the impact that may result from the changes in governmental regulation under different political administrations. Changes in regulations, the imposition of additional regulations, or the enactment of new legislation that impacts employment, labor, trade, transportation or logistics, health care, tax or environmental issues could have a material adverse impact on our financial condition or results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A privacy breach could adversely affect or business</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The protection of customer, employee and company data is critical. The regulatory environment surrounding information security and privacy is demanding, with the frequent imposition of new and changing requirements. In addition, customers have a high expectation that we will adequately protect their personal information. A significant breach of customer, employee or company data could damage our reputation, result in lost sales, fines or lawsuits or have a material adverse impact on our financial condition or results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Damage or interruptions to our information and computer systems or the inability to implement new technologies effectively could disrupt our business or reduce our sales or profitability</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We rely extensively on various information systems, data centers and software applications to manage many aspects of our business, including to process and record transactions in our stores, to enable effective communications systems, to plan and track inventory flow and to generate performance and financial reports.&#160;&#160;We are dependent on the integrity, security and consistent operations of these systems and related back-up systems.&#160;&#160;Our computer systems are subject to damage or interruption from power outages, computer and telecommunications failures, computer viruses, security breaches, catastrophic events such as fires, floods, earthquakes, tornadoes, hurricanes, acts of war or terrorism and usage errors by our associates or contractors.&#160;&#160;The efficient operation and successful growth of our business depends upon these information systems, including our ability to operate them effectively and to select and implement appropriate new technologies systems, controls, data centers and adequate disaster recovery system successfully.&#160;&#160;For example, in 2011 we plan to upgrade our Allocation system in order to improve our ability to get the right product into the right store at the right time.</font></div>

In addition, under the &#8220;net&#8221; terms of all leases, the Company pays maintenance expenses, real estate taxes and other charges. The leases for most of our stores also provide for contingent rent based upon a percentage of sales in excess of certain thresholds. Minimum rental payments for leased locations aggregated approximately $35,684,000 and $27,060,000 for fiscal 2010 and 2009, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Company does not assume the obligation to update any forward-looking statement.&#160;&#160;Shareholders should carefully evaluate such statements in light of factors, including risk factors, described in the Company&#8217;s filings with the SEC, especially on Forms 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K.&#160;&#160;In Item 1A., &#8220;Risk Factors&#8221; of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, the Company discusses in more detail various important risk factors that could cause actual results to differ from expected or historic results.&#160;&#160;The Company notes these factors for readers as permitted by the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995.&#160;&#160;Shareholders should understand that it is not possible to predict or identify all such factors.&#160;&#160;Consequently, shareholders should not consider any such list to be a complete statement of all potential risks or uncertainties.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America requires the appropriate application of certain accounting policies, many of which require us to make estimates and assumptions about future events and their impact on amounts reported in the financial statements and related notes.&#160;&#160;Since future events and their impact cannot be determined with certainty, the actual results will inevitably differ from the Company&#8217;s estimates.&#160;&#160;Such differences could be material to the financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Company believes that its application of accounting policies, and the estimates inherently required by the policies, are reasonable. These accounting policies and estimates are constantly reevaluated, and adjustments are made when facts and circumstances dictate a change.&#160;&#160;Historically, the Company has found the application of accounting policies to be appropriate, and actual results have not differed materially from those determined using necessary estimates.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Company&#8217;s accounting policies are more fully described in Note 1 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements presented elsewhere in this Annual Report.&#160;&#160;The Company has identified certain critical accounting policies that are described below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Merchandise Invento</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">r</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">y</font> &#8211; Merchandise inventories are stated at the lower of cost or market on a first-in, first-out (FIFO) basis, as determined by the retail inventory method.&#160;&#160;Under the retail method, inventory cost and the resulting gross margins are calculated by applying a cost to retail ratio between the costs of goods available for sale and the retail value of inventories.&#160;&#160;For a brief period, from October 4, 2009 through October 2, 2010, the Syms stores utilized a different method, the moving weighted average cost method.&#160;&#160;Under the moving weighted average cost method, inventory cost and the resulting gross margins are calculated by applying an average cost based on the cost of goods available for sale divided by the number of units available for sale.&#160;&#160;After we completed the acquisition of Filene&#8217;s, the Company found itself in the position that a portion of its business was utilizing the moving average cost method and a portion of its business was utilizing the retail inventory method.&#160;&#160;The Company thus was faced with the choice of either converting Filene&#8217;s to the moving average cost method or transitioning the Syms stores back to the system that they had previously utilized.&#160;&#160;The Company determined that it would be more effective to revert back to the retail inventory method.&#160;&#160;The change in the method of recording Syms inventory in the third quarter of fiscal 2009 and the third quarter of fiscal 2010 did not have a material impact on reported results of operations.&#160;&#160;The significant estimates used are for markdowns and shrinkage.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Factors considered in the determination of permanent markdowns include current and anticipated demand, customer preferences and age of the merchandise, fashion trends and weather conditions.&#160;&#160;In addition, inventory is also evaluated against corporate pre-determined historical markdown trends.&#160;&#160;When a decision is made to permanently markdown merchandise, the resulting gross margin reduction is recognized in the period the markdown is recorded.&#160;&#160;The timing of the decision, particularly surrounding the balance sheet date, can have a significant effect on the results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Shrinkage is estimated as a percentage of sales for the period from the date of the last physical inventory to the end of the fiscal year.&#160;&#160;Physical inventories are taken at least annually for all stores and inventory records are adjusted accordingly.&#160;&#160;The shrinkage rate from the most recent physical inventory, in combination with historical experience, is used as the standard for the shrinkage accrual following the physical inventory.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Company has found the use of these estimates to be appropriate and actual results have not differed materially.&#160;&#160;However, the Company is subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause its future estimates to differ materially from past experience.</font></div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">13</font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Long-Lived Assets</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic"> -</font>In evaluating and measuring an impairment loss, we consider individual retail locations to be the appropriate asset group, since the store level is the lowest level at which identifiable cash flows are independent of the cash flows of other assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;We evaluate long lived assets for impairment at all of our retail locations on at least an annual basis at the end of each fiscal year, after the holiday selling season, when we have the most visibility into the operations of the individual store.&#160;&#160;We will also test an asset group for impairment during the year if any impairment indicators are identified that could result in a potential impairment.&#160;&#160;If it is determined that such indicators are present and the review discloses that the assets will not be fully recoverable, based on undiscounted estimated cash flows over the remaining useful lives, their carrying values are reduced to estimated fair value.&#160;&#160;Various factors, including future sales growth and profit margins, are included in this analysis.&#160;&#160;To the extent these future projections or the Company&#8217;s strategies change, the conclusion regarding impairment may differ from the Company&#8217;s current estimates.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deferred Tax Valuation Allowance</font> &#8211; The Company has considered future taxable income and ongoing prudent and feasible tax planning strategies that could produce additional future taxable income in assessing the need for a valuation allowance.&#160;&#160;Should the Company determine that it will not be able to realize all or part of our net deferred tax asset in the future, an adjustment to the deferred tax asset will be charged to income in the period such determination is made.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Results of Operations</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The following discussion compares the fiscal years ended February 26, 2011, February 27, 2010 and February 28, 2009. All of the fiscal years were comprised of 52 weeks.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Fiscal Year Ended February 26, 2011 (Fiscal 2010) Compared to Fiscal Year Ended February 27, 2010 (Fiscal 2009)</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Net sales increased by $67.8 million or 18% to $445.1 million during fiscal 2010 from $377.3 million in fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;This increase was primarily the result of having a full 12 months of sales in Fiscal 2010 from the Filene&#8217;s stores which were acquired in fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;&#160;Net sales in fiscal 2009 included sales from Filene&#8217;s from June 19, 2009 (first day of operating ownership).&#160;&#160;Comparable store sales, including Filene&#8217;s sales for comparable periods, were flat in fiscal 2010.&#160;&#160;Comparable store sales in the prior year, excluding Filene&#8217;s sales, decreased 15%.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s comparable store sales computation only includes stores that have been owned and operated by the Company for a period of at least twelve full fiscal months.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company opened one store during fiscal 2010 which contributed $1.9 million of the sales increase.&#160;&#160;Partially offsetting the above sales increases was the loss of $24.7 million of sales in fiscal 2010 resulting from the closing of four stores during fiscal 2010 and five stores during fiscal 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>By merchandise category, our Women&#8217;s business grew to 46% of total company net sales from 44% in the prior year, Domestics grew to 6% from 5% last year and Shoes grew to 5% from 4% in fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;This was primarily the result of having a full 12 months of sales in fiscal 2010 from the Filene&#8217;s stores which were acquired in fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;These increases came at the expense of Men&#8217;s which decreased 4%, from 42% of total Company net sales in fiscal 2009 to 38% this year.&#160;&#160;Children&#8217;s apparel did not change, remaining at 5% of total company net sales.&#160;&#160;Comparable store sales for the stores in the New York metropolitan area were negative low single digits.&#160;&#160;Offsetting this were the stores in the South that had flat comparable store sales and stores in other areas of the country that had comparable store sales increase in the low single digits.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Gross profit increased by $28.7 million to $173.8 million during fiscal 2010 from $145.1 million during fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;This increase was primarily the result of having a full 12 months of sales in fiscal 2010 from the Filene&#8217;s stores which were acquired in fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;Gross profit as a percent of net sales increased 50 basis points to 39.0% during fiscal 2010 from 38.5% during the comparable prior year period.&#160;&#160;This increase was primarily due to the Company taking fewer markdowns this year as a result of it being less promotional.&#160;&#160;Partially offsetting the lower markdowns, the Company increased its reserve for inventory obsolescence by $6.2 million, as it determined that it had not adequately cleared out old season merchandise as of year-end.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company&#8217;s leased department income increased during fiscal 2010.&#160;&#160;Partially offsetting these increases were a lower markup, as the Company continued to reduce prices in order to maintain competitiveness with other retailers.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The Company&#8217;s gross profit excludes the cost of its distribution network.&#160;&#160;For the fiscal years ended February 26, 2011 and February 27, 2010, the amounts incurred for our distribution network that were classified in selling, general and administrative expenses and occupancy costs were $19.0 million and $15.6 million, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Selling, general and administrative expense (&#8220;SG&amp;A&#8221;) increased $14.9 million to $124.4 million during fiscal 2010 as compared to $109.5 million during fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;This increase was primarily the result of having a full 12 months of expenses in fiscal 2010 from the Filene&#8217;s stores, which were acquired in fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;As a percent of net sales, SG&amp;A decreased approximately 110 basis points to 27.9% of net sales during fiscal 2010 from 29.0% of net sales in the comparable prior year period.&#160;&#160;SG&amp;A as a percent of net sales decreased primarily as a result of lower payroll expenses as a percent of net sales during fiscal 2010.&#160;&#160;In addition, the prior year period included life insurance premiums on the policy covering the Company&#8217;s founder prior to his death in November 2009.</font></div>

</div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Advertising expense for fiscal 2010 was $7.0 million or 1.6% of net sales as compared to $8.2 million or 2.2% of net sales for fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;Advertising expense for fiscal 2010 decreased primarily due to the Company being less promotional this year, a reallocation of advertising efforts to less expensive social media from more traditional media and the fact that the Company incurred expenses celebrating Filene&#8217;s 100<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">th</font> anniversary and Syms&#8217; 50<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">th</font> anniversary in fiscal 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Occupancy costs, net, were $64.2 million or 14.4% of net sales for fiscal 2010 as compared to $49.5 million or 13.1% of net sales for fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;This increase was primarily the result of having a full 12 months of occupancy costs in fiscal 2010 from the Filene&#8217;s stores which were acquired in fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;Partially offsetting this increase was the closing of four stores during fiscal 2010 and five stores during fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;&#160;The Company reduces its net occupancy costs by the amount of&#160;&#160;rental income from third parties on real estate holdings incidental to the Company&#8217;s retail operations.&#160;&#160;That factor did not materially impact comparative results during fiscal 2010.&#160;&#160;For fiscal 2010 and fiscal 2009, rental income was $2.3 million and $2.4 million, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Depreciation and amortization expense was $14.6 million or 3.3% of net sales for fiscal 2010 as compared to $11.4 million or 3.0% of net sales for fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;The increase in depreciation and amortization expense was primarily a result of the Filene&#8217;s acquisition and capital expenditure additions during the past two fiscal years.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Asset impairment charge for fiscal 2010 was $4.3 million or 1.0% of net sales as compared to $0.1 million or 0.0% of net sales for fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;During fiscal 2010, the Company determined that six stores&#8217; long-lived assets had been impaired.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company shifted most of its merchandise processing from its New Jersey distribution center to its Massachusetts distribution center, in order to reduce distribution costs.&#160;&#160;This shift resulted in a partial impairment of the New Jersey facility.&#160;&#160;In conjunction with this move, an office in Massachusetts was closed giving rise to a further impairment charge.&#160;&#160;During fiscal 2009, one store&#8217;s long-lived assets had been determined to be impaired.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In conjunction with the acquisition of Filene&#8217;s in June 2009, the Company determined that the fair values of assets acquired exceeded the purchase price by approximately $9.7 million, resulting in a bargain purchase gain in fiscal 2009, based upon valuations of inventory, fixed assets, equipment and intangible assets net of deferred taxes, customer obligations and other adjustments.&#160;&#160;Acquisition costs of $4.9 million, including investment banking, legal, professional and other costs, were expensed in fiscal 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Other income was $0 for fiscal 2010 as compared to $25.0 million for fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;Last year&#8217;s income resulted from a gain on life insurance proceeds from officers&#8217; life insurance policies on the Company&#8217;s founder, who passed away during fiscal 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Loss on disposition of assets for fiscal 2010 was $0.5 million or 0.1% of net sales as compared to $1.2 million or 0.3% of net sales for fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;During fiscal 2010 the loss on disposition of assets was the net result of closing four stores, selling three stores and downsizing one store.&#160;&#160;The related charge in fiscal 2009 was related to the closure of five stores.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The Company recorded $9.3 million of restructuring charges during fiscal 2010 and had no such charges in fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;The Company opened one store and closed four stores during fiscal 2010.&#160;&#160;The Company is required to continue to make lease payments on two of these closed stores, one through May 2012 and the other through September 2017.&#160;&#160;The Company has recorded the present value of these payments as a restructuring charge, totaling approximately $7.2 million.&#160;&#160;In addition, as part of the integration of the Syms and Filene&#8217;s operations, a total of $2.1 million of IT related professional fees, legal fees and severance costs associated with staffing level reductions were incurred and have been recorded as restructuring charges.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Interest expense was $1.4 million or 0.3% of net sales during fiscal 2010 compared to $1.5 million or 0.4% of net sales during fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;For fiscal 2010, interest expense was a result of borrowings on the Company&#8217;s revolving credit facility.&#160;&#160;During the prior year period, interest expense was due to borrowings against the cash surrender value of officers&#8217; life insurance policies and borrowings on the Company&#8217;s revolving credit facility.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The sales and gross profit increase attributable to the acquisition of Filene&#8217;s were insufficient to offset the expense increases and impairment and restructuring charges incurred during fiscal 2010.&#160;&#160;As a result of the above-noted items, the loss before income taxes for fiscal 2010 was $51.7 million as compared to a loss of $6.4 million for fiscal 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>For fiscal 2010, the effective income tax rate was 36.5% as compared to 230.2% for fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;In fiscal 2010, the difference between the effective income tax rate and the federal statutory rate resulted primarily from state income taxes, adjustments related to prior year income taxes, and to a lesser extent permanent differences in the deductibility of expenses for book and tax.&#160;&#160;In fiscal 2009, this difference related mostly to the non-taxable nature of the life insurance proceeds received and recorded in income, partially offset by the effect of adjustments related to prior year taxes.&#160;&#160;The change in the effective income tax rate is primarily due to the above noted items occurring in one year and not the other.</font></div>
